concept.name: Initiative selling
concept.definition: In Market Profile/auction terminology, initiative selling is aggressive selling occurring at or below the established value area — 'unexpected' activity in which sellers hit bids through accepted value to force the auction toward new, lower value. It is the selling side of other-timeframe participation that breaks balance downward.
concept.intuition: Initiative sellers do not wait for a better price — they sell into and below value because they believe lower prices are coming.
concept.mechanics: Identified by selling at/below the prior VAL with conviction evidence: downside range extension, one-time-framing lower, and footprint signs such as stacked sell imbalances and negative delta.
concept.failure_modes: Same dependence on correctly drawn value as initiative buying; initiative selling into a supported low is frequently absorbed, producing the sharp failed-auction reversals that trap late sellers.
concept.misconceptions: Initiative selling is not proof of informed distribution — it can be capitulation by weak hands at exactly the wrong moment, and only subsequent acceptance or rejection distinguishes the two.
concept.example: After opening below the prior VAL, sellers press through the first two brackets with expanding negative delta and range extension; the tape is read as initiative selling and rallies are sold rather than dips bought.

citations.source: FuturesIndicators — Trading With Market Profile: Practical Setups (responsive vs initiative activity)
